newsitem.title: CHINA: China city in confusion over fire that kills 39.
newsitem.headline: China city in confusion over fire that kills 39.

text.p: A fire that raged through a hotel in central China has killed at least 39 people and seriously injured dozens, many hurt when they leapt from windows to escape the flames and smoke, state media said on Thursday.
However, police at the scene of the blaze in Changsha, capital of central Hunan province, said only eight people had been killed.

Police said the manager of a privately contracted restaurant on the second floor of the Yanshan Hotel in Changsha had been detained in connection with the blaze, but arson was not suspected. Two other managers had been arrested.

The death toll had risen to 39 from the fire that started in the second floor seafood restaurant and roared up to the seventh floor of the hotel in the early hours of Wednesday, said one government official who declined to be identified.
Many of the 172 guests and 30 staff in the building were asleep when the fire began.

State television said at least 49 people had been injured in the blaze, the deadliest reported in China since a blaze in December 1994 in a cinema in the northwestern Xinjiang region killed 323 people, most of them children.
Some 28 of the injured were in serious condition, the government official said.

A spokesman for the Changsha Public Security Bureau said the fire killed eight people and left 31 seriously injured, some hurt when they leapt from upper-floor windows to escape. The restaurant had received two warnings to improve its fire safety precautions, an official said.
Confusion over the casualty toll underlined China's lack of facilities in many rural cities for dealing with disasters as well as an official reluctance to publicise bad news.

Officials said 21 fire engines and 1,000 police and firefighters rushed to the scene, but rescuers had difficulty extinguishing the fire because of single-storey buildings clustered around the base of the hotel.
Many guests jumped from upper floor windows as the flames and smoke roared through the hotel, blocking exits on all six of the burning floors, officials said.
"I saw the whole thing," the police official said. "About 30 people jumped out of the windows on the top floors but none of them were killed because they wrapped themselves in quilts."
The Hunan Number One hospital had admitted 22 victims, of whom 13 were dead on arrival, most from smoke inhalation.
"In the burns ward we have people who were burnt and we have people with internal injuries from jumping out of upper stories," a nurse at the Hunan Number Two hospital said late on Wednesday.
"There are also people with broken bones who jumped out of windows. There are rather a lot of patients with broken bones," she said.

China implemented safety measures in hotels, restaurants and cinemas in 1995, sharply cutting the number of major fires after a string of fire disasters in 1994 killed 2,600 people and injured 4,000, making it China's deadliest year on record.
